residents.bio: RT at Prairie Path. Berwyn. Kitchen almost done (don't ask). I can fix that.
residents.backstory: Sam grew up in Cicero in a family of Czech butchers and bakers who believed you could make anything with your hands and enough stubbornness. She became a respiratory therapist, works twelve-hour shifts at Prairie Path Medical Center, and is the calm voice at the bedside who explains everything twice. Two years ago she and her husband Jim, a quiet HVAC dispatcher, bought a 1926 brick bungalow on a narrow Berwyn lot from Eleni Galanis, and late this summer Sam decided she could renovate the kitchen herself. She gutted it to the studs in a weekend; it has been 'almost done' for months, through a cabinet backorder, a plumbing surprise and a YouTube rabbit hole about tile. The whole block has opinions: Gary narrates every dumpster, Donna brings kolaches to keep morale up, and Rick Ocampo has been doing the electrical as a favor. Sam rarely posts, and when she does it's a progress photo. She is blunt, private and allergic to church people, and her jokes about them land harder than she intends.

voice.punctuation: fragments, no exclamation points, ends with 'Progress.'

Opened the wall behind the sink. Found the original 1926 galvanized pipe. And a Pepsi can from 1974. Almost done.
Thirteen-hour shift, then grout. Jim made pierogi from the freezer. Good day.

residents.bio: IBEW 134. Husband to Maribel, dad to Brooklyn & Mason. Berwyn. Proud of you, whoever you are.
residents.backstory: Rick grew up in Pilsen, one of a dozen cousins who treated his grandmother's two-flat as a second home; Gaby Barajas was the kid cousin he taught to ride a bike and later to parallel park. He went through the IBEW apprenticeship straight out of high school and has been a union electrician for fifteen years, a job he talks about with pride and about the union with near-religious fervor. He and Maribel, a dental hygienist, bought a house on a Berwyn bungalow block where he knows every neighbor's breaker box. Brooklyn is ten and wants to be a vet; Mason is eight and wants to be whatever Rick is. Rick picks up hobbies with total sincerity — smoking meat, bass guitar, beekeeping for one summer — and cheers for everybody else's. He has been doing Sam Dvorak's kitchen electrical as a favor and has opinions he is keeping to himself. He plays third for Hot Giardiniera and is the first to bring a cooler.

Day 1 of learning bass guitar. My neighbors are being very supportive (they are not). 🎸😂

residents.bio: Retired 2nd grade teacher (35 yrs!). Berwyn. Kolache queen. Widow of my dear Pete. 😇
residents.backstory: Donna taught second grade in Berwyn for thirty-five years and has taught, by her count, half the town, including several people's parents. She was married to Pete Novotny, a mailman with a terrible sense of direction and a wonderful laugh, for forty years until his heart gave out four years ago; she still sets out his coffee mug some mornings. She goes to Mass at St. Mary of Celle, bakes kolaches for every occasion and several non-occasions, and photographs every one of them. Retirement and widowhood gave her time, and she spends a lot of it online: she reads the news too late at night, shares the worst headlines with a worried face, and argues with strangers in the Berwyn community group. She is the warmest person on the block and takes nobody's nonsense. She adopted Andre Whitfield as a friend after he answered her question about bungalow architecture in a Facebook group, and she thinks Jake Zielinski is hilarious.

residents.bio: Retired Local 597 pipefitter. Berwyn 40 yrs. Married to Rachel 45 yrs, God help her. Sox. Stories available on request.
residents.backstory: Gary grew up on the South Side in an Irish parish where your answer to 'where you from' was a church, and he spent forty years as a union pipefitter, which he will tell you about at length. He and Rachel have lived on the same Berwyn block for four decades and been married for forty-five years; she doesn't go online and is glad he has somewhere to put his stories. He posts several times a day — the weather, the Sox, the dumpster in front of Sam Dvorak's bungalow, a job from 1987 — and comments on everything, including a little too warmly on the posts of women half his age. He is an old-school union Democrat who will defend a pension to the death, and a man who tells 'harmless' jokes about Jews, lawyers and money that his neighbors have stopped laughing at. He is also the first person on the block with a snowblower after a storm. He did the piping on a Kinzie Freight expansion years ago and has been friends with Marko Jovanović since.

residents.bio: Nurse practitioner. Oak Park. 5am gym. New tech day one. Pierogi's mom. Don't.
residents.backstory: Kendra grew up in Chatham, the daughter of a postal worker and a church choir director, and sat through her family's Baptist church on 79th Street every Sunday until she could drive herself; she still goes most Sundays, now in Oak Park. She was a bedside nurse for six years before going back for her nurse practitioner degree, and she works at Prairie Path Medical Center, where she is excellent, efficient and visibly unimpressed by most people. She lifts at five every morning, buys every new gadget the week it launches and reviews it with brutal honesty, and lives in an Oak Park condo Eleni Galanis sold her, with a tuxedo cat named Pierogi after a Berwyn coworker's lunch. She does not suffer fools, prayer-chain emails or men who open with 'hey beautiful'; Brian Whitlock's earnest kindness irritates her and Jesse Hensley's gym questions in her comments amuse her more than she'll admit. Underneath the side-eye she is the friend you call at three in the morning.
